question: What are the Table A minimum power line clearance distances for each voltage range?

body.text:
Table A, line voltage in kV AC, then minimum feet:
• Up to 50: 10
• Over 50 to 200: 15
• Over 200 to 350: 20
• Over 350 to 500: 25
• Over 500 to 750: 35
• Over 750 to 1,000: 45
up to 50 | 10 over 50 to 200 | 15 over 200 to 350 | 20 over 350 to 500 | 25 over 500 to 750 | 35 over 750 to 1,000 | 45
Over 1,000 kV has no fixed number in the table. The distance must be established by one of these:
over 1,000 | (as established by the utility owner/operator or registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution)

question: If the voltage is exactly on a Table A breakpoint, like 50, 200, or 350 kV, which row do I use?

body.text:
Use the row that ends with that number. The upper value is included in its row:
• 50 kV: 10 feet
• 200 kV: 15 feet
• 350 kV: 20 feet
• 500 kV: 25 feet
• 750 kV: 35 feet
• 1,000 kV: 45 feet
Anything above a breakpoint moves to the next row.
The value that follows “to” is up to and includes that value.
up to 50 | 10 over 50 to 200 | 15 over 200 to 350 | 20 over 350 to 500 | 25 over 500 to 750 | 35 over 750 to 1,000 | 45

question: If I don't know the line voltage, can I still use Table A or assume 10 feet?

body.text: No. Table A can't be applied without the voltage. Option (3) requires determining it.
Determine the line's voltage and the minimum approach distance permitted under Table A
The employer has other choices. One is confirmed deenergizing with visible grounding at the worksite.
Another is the 20-foot option with its encroachment precautions. This section is limited to lines up to 350 kV, so make sure the line isn't above that.
Ensure that no part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), gets closer than 20 feet to the power line
Practice: don't guess voltage from how the poles or wires look.

question: If the crane could get closer than the Table A distance, what has to be done to use Option (3)?

body.text: All the encroachment prevention requirements in paragraph (b) apply, to keep everything from getting closer than the Table A distance.
the employer must follow the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section
These include a planning meeting, non-conductive tag lines if tag lines are used, and an elevated warning line, barricade or sign line.

At least one added measure is also required: proximity alarm, dedicated spotter, automatic warning device, range limiter, or insulating link/device. Each has its own conditions. An unseen warning line triggers extra spotter requirements. Paragraph (b)(4) does not apply to subpart V work.

question: Where does the warning line go when I'm using Table A?

body.text: When encroachment precautions are required under Option (3), put it at the Table A minimum approach distance from the power line. For Option (2), it goes at 20 feet. question: How is the Table A distance used to decide whether equipment can be below a power line?

body.text: The baseline: no part of the equipment, load line or load may be below a line unless the employer has confirmed the utility deenergized it and visibly grounded it at the worksite, or an exception applies.
For a non-extensible boom, one exception checks the equipment's uppermost part with the boom at true vertical.
would be more than 20 feet below the plane of the power line or more than the Table A of this section minimum clearance distance below the plane of the power line.

For articulating or extensible booms, such as hydraulic telescoping or knuckle booms, make the same check with the boom fully extended at true vertical. The employer must demonstrate the exception applies. Subpart V work and demonstrated infeasibility meeting § 1926.1410 are the other exceptions.
with the boom in the fully extended position, at true vertical
